title: Workout Planner and Progress Tracker App

prd.oneLiner: Connect goals, workout routines, set and rep logs, personal records, recovery notes, and progress insights in one fitness-tracking flow.
prd.goal: Help people improve weekly workout-plan completion and clearly see training progress over time.
prd.whyNow: Workout routines, set logs, personal records, and recovery notes are scattered across apps, notes, and memory, making progressive training difficult to sustain.
prd.problem: Workout routines, set logs, personal records, and recovery notes are scattered across apps, notes, and memory, making progressive training difficult to sustain.
prd.solution: Connect goals, workout routines, set and rep logs, personal records, recovery notes, and progress insights in one fitness-tracking flow.
prd.alternatives: Notes, spreadsheets, general-purpose apps, and single-purpose trackers
prd.differentiator: Connect personal goals, records, and progress so the next action is clear.

targets.name: Individual planning workouts and logging exercise progress
targets.needs: Capture personal goals and records quickly and know the next action.
targets.pain: Workout routines, set logs, personal records, and recovery notes are scattered across apps, notes, and memory, making progressive training difficult to sustain.

scenarios.text: A person sets a goal and reminder preferences.
A person completes the core action or adds a record and checks progress.
A person reviews weekly insights and adjusts the next action and reminders.
A person exports their data or changes sharing boundaries.

prd.northStar: Share of active users completing their planned weekly action

kpis.name: First-week core-action completion
kpis.target: Help people improve weekly workout-plan completion and clearly see training progress over time.
kpis.method: Share of new users completing the core action or record within seven days

kpis.name: Weekly return rate
kpis.method: Share of users recording, reviewing, or adjusting reminders each week

kpis.name: User data-control completion
kpis.method: Completion history for export, deletion, and sharing-setting changes

inScope: Fitness goal, routine, exercise, set, repetition, and weight entry
Today's workout, exercise history, personal record, weekly volume, and goal-progress lookup
Workout-session start, set logging, workout completion, routine adjustment, and recovery-note handling
Workout frequency, training volume, personal record, goal progress, and streak reporting
Fitness goal, routine, exercise, set, repetition, and weight entry validation and draft saving
Personal record search, filters, and history
Onboarding, empty states, and return-use guidance
nonGoals: Operating regulated financial, health, or employment services
Sharing personal data without explicit user consent
assumptions: Users manage their own profile and record data.
Notifications and optional data connections require explicit consent.
risks: Incomplete personal records can weaken progress insights.
Exposure of sensitive personal data can reduce trust and retention.
openQuestions: What first-week action makes the value clear to a new user?
Which reminders and data connections must remain opt-in?
constraints: Users must be able to export and delete their records.
Sensitive data follows data minimization and explicit consent.
Reminders, sharing, and external data connections require explicit consent.
